test_cases.question: Why is database replication used?
test_cases.ground_truth_answer: Database replication is used to protect against data loss during system failures, handle increased traffic by scaling reads horizontally, and improve latency by routing user requests to the physically closest regional node.

sources.quote: to protect against data loss during system failures to serve increased traffic or even to improve latency when pursuing a regional strategy

artifacts.location: Page 1 & 2 (Section 2: Why Database Replication is Essential)
key_points: Protecting Against Data Loss: Ensures high durability by maintaining redundant copies of the dataset.
Serving Increased Traffic: Enables horizontal read scaling by separating write operations from read operations.
Improving Latency (Regional Strategy): Geographic distribution allows routing client requests to the physically closest node.
Mitigates single point of failure (SPOF) risks of a single node.
Resolves regional latency issues for global database users.

required_concepts: durability / preventing data loss / fault tolerance

test_cases.question: What architecture is shown when replication is discussed?
test_cases.ground_truth_answer: The primary architecture shown is the Leader-Follower (also known as Primary-Replica) model. In this setup, all write transactions are sent to a single designated leader database, which processes them locally and then propagates the updates to follower replicas. Clients can read from any of the followers.

sources.quote: first there is the leader follower strategy also known as primary replica this is probably the most common strategy where a query writes to a single designated leader the leader then replicates the updated data to followers

key_points: Leader-Follower (Primary-Replica): Writes are routed exclusively to a single, designated leader database; updates cascade to followers.

artifacts.location: Page 1 & 2 (Recommended Architectural Model & Node Roles Table)
key_points: Recommended Model: Primary -> Replicas setup where primary accepts writes and replicas serve read requests.

required_concepts: Writes processed by a single leader / primary

test_cases.question: How does the architecture address the scalability problem?
test_cases.ground_truth_answer: Replication addresses the scalability problem by separating read and write workloads. Rather than forcing a single node to handle both, high-volume read traffic is routed to horizontal follower replicas, offloading the primary leader so it can focus entirely on write operations.

sources.quote: asynchronous replication may be an option for use cases where transaction speed is more important... proactive strategy to help applications scale

key_points: Enables horizontal read scaling by allowing write operations to be separated from read operations.
Offloads read queries to geographically near replicas to handle high-volume traffic with minimal latency.
Isolates read traffic to dedicated replicas, shielding the primary from high concurrent read load.

required_concepts: horizontal scaling / offloading read traffic to replicas
preventing the primary/leader node from being overwhelmed
